result.title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
result.summary: What should ``verified'' mean when evaluating LLM-generated code? Many existing pipelines report a single verification number. We argue this collapses three distinct properties measured in a conditional audit sequence: verifier acceptance (Surface A), \emph{syntactic specification binding (Surface B: does the proof obligation bind to the spec?), and \emph{semantic specification fidelity} (Surface C: does the spec capture the informal requirement?). Two empirical demonstrations show the surfaces separate. \textbf{First ($A \neq B$), via Li@Opus (a same-model reproduction of \citet{li2025dafny}'s Dafny-as-intermediate-representation (IR) pipeline under Claude Opus 4.7) on three Python benchmarks}: it reaches \textbf{99.1\% verifier acceptance} on HumanEval while only \textbf{1.9\%} carry a certificate binding to a spec-defined predicate or function. \textbf{Second ($B \neq C$), via VCG on two Rust benchmarks}: we use VCG (which is our own in-house Dafny-as-intermediate pipeline) on Rust because the Rust target lets us enforce fully-verifiable output (every component ships as a Dafny certificate, ensures-binding gate passing by construction). Even inside that construction, \textbf{11.48\% (MBPP-Rust) and 14.82\% (VeriContest LC slice) of structurally-verified samples still fail hidden tests}. On the LC slice of VeriContest, \textbf{VCG's reported End2End rate is 7.79\% (535/6870).} The cited external rates are 5.51\% (GPT-5.5) and 1.88\% (single-shot Opus 4.7). These give descriptive differences of 2.3 percentage points and 4.14$\times$, respectively; task-budget, repair and harness differences prevent a matched-performance claim.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张 LLM 生成代码的「已验证」应拆成三个可分离层面——验证器接受、证明义务与 spec 的语法绑定、spec 对非形式需求的语义保真，并用 Dafny 作为中间表示的管线在 Python 与 Rust 基准上给出 A≠B、B≠C 的实证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「通过检查≠真正绑定到需求」的分层审计思路，可能类比 LVR 中「答案正确但未实际使用 latent 状态或视觉证据」的鉴别性评价，可供核查；但论文不涉及视觉输入、推理状态或训练监督，联系仅为评价概念层面。
